title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第十一 薛李二劉高徐
title.en: Volume 86 Biographies 11: Xue, Li, Er, Liu Gao, Xu
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第十一 薛李二劉高徐 Volume 86 Biographies 11: Xue, Li, Er, Liu Gao, Xu

sentences.zh: 薛李二劉高徐

translations.literal: Xue, Li, the two Liu's, Gao, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue [Ju], Li [Gui], the two [families named] Liu, Gao [Shilian], and Xu [Yuanlang].

sentences.zh: 薛舉，蘭州金城人。

translations.literal: Xue Ju was a native of Jincheng in Lan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju came from Jincheng in Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁岸，武敢善射。

translations.literal: His appearance was towering; he was bold in combat and skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in stature, fearless in battle, and an excellent archer.

sentences.zh: 殖產巨萬，好結納邊豪，為長雄。

translations.literal: He amassed wealth in the tens of thousands, delighted in befriending frontier magnates, and became a local chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: He built a fortune of many millions, cultivated ties with powerful border figures, and came to dominate the region.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末任金城府校尉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui Daye era he served as captain of Jincheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Emperor Yang's Daye reign he held the post of captain in the Jincheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 會歲兇，隴西盜起，金城令郝瑗將討賊，募兵數千，檄舉將。

translations.literal: When famine struck, bandits rose in Longxi; the magistrate of Jincheng, Hao Yuan, was about to campaign against them, recruited several thousand troops, and summoned Ju as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: A year of famine brought banditry to Longxi. Hao Yuan, magistrate of Jincheng, raised several thousand men to suppress the rebels and appointed Xue Ju to lead them.

sentences.zh: 始授甲，大會置酒，舉與子仁杲及其黨劫瑗於坐，矯稱捕反者，即起兵，囚郡縣官，發粟以賑貧乏，自號西秦霸王，建元秦興，以仁杲為齊公，少子仁越為晉公。

translations.literal: When armor was first issued, at a great assembly with wine set out, Ju with his son Rengao and their faction seized Yuan at the feast, falsely claiming they were arresting rebels; they immediately raised troops, imprisoned prefectural and county officials, distributed grain to relieve the poor, styled himself Hegemon-King of Western Qin, adopted the era name Qinxing, made Rengao Duke of Qi, and his younger son Renyue Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At the first issue of arms, during a grand banquet, Xue Ju, his son Rengao, and their followers seized Hao Yuan in his seat, pretending they were rounding up traitors. They rose at once, locked up the local officials, opened the granaries for the destitute, and proclaimed himself Hegemon-King of Western Qin with the era name Qinxing. Rengao became Duke of Qi and his younger son Renyue Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 它賊宗羅睺帥眾下之，以為義興公。

translations.literal: Another bandit leader, Zong Luohou, brought his forces to submit and was made Duke of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw Zong Luohou came in with his men and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 更招附余盜，剽馬牧。

translations.literal: He further recruited remaining bandits and raided horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: He drew in more scattered rebels and raided the horse herds of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 兵鋒銳甚，所徇皆下。

translations.literal: His army's edge was exceedingly sharp; wherever he marched, all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His troops fought with devastating force, and every place he marched fell to him.

sentences.zh: 隋將皇甫綰兵萬人屯枹罕，舉以精卒二千襲之，遇於赤岸。

translations.literal: The Sui general Huangfu Wan stationed ten thousand men at Fuhan; Ju struck with two thousand elite troops and met him at Chian.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui commander Huangfu Wan held Fuhan with ten thousand men. Xue Ju hit him with two thousand picked troops and engaged him at Red Bank.

sentences.zh: 大風且澍，逆舉陣，綰不擊。

translations.literal: A great wind blew with driving rain against Ju's formation; Wan did not attack.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind and downpour blew straight into Xue Ju's lines, and Huangfu Wan held his men back.

sentences.zh: 俄反風綰屯，氣色曀冥，部伍錯亂，舉介騎先眾乘之，綰陣大潰，進陷枹罕。

translations.literal: Soon the wind reversed against Wan's camp; the sky grew dark and murky, ranks fell into disorder; Ju, armored and on horseback, led the van ahead of the host and pressed the attack; Wan's formation collapsed utterly, and Ju advanced to take Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the wind swung around into Huangfu Wan's camp. The sky turned black, his ranks broke apart, and Xue Ju, in full armor at the head of his cavalry, charged in ahead of the main body. Wan's army was routed completely, and Xue Ju pressed on to capture Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 岷山羌鐘利俗以眾二萬降，舉大振。

translations.literal: Zhong Lisu of the Minshan Qiang submitted with twenty thousand men, and Ju's power greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Lisu of the Minshan Qiang came over with twenty thousand followers, and Xue Ju's fortunes soared.

sentences.zh: 進仁杲為齊王、東道行軍元帥，羅睺為義興王副之；

translations.literal: He advanced Rengao to King of Qi and Grand Marshal of the Eastern Route Army, with Luohou as King of Yixing to assist him;
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Rengao to King of Qi and supreme commander of the eastern campaign, with Luohou as King of Yixing as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 仁越晉王、河州刺史。

translations.literal: Renyue was made King of Jin and prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renyue became King of Jin and prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 因徇下鄯、廓二州。

translations.literal: He then marched to reduce Shan and Kuo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He swept on to subdue Shan and Kuo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 不闋旬，盡有隴西地，眾十三萬。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he held all of Longxi, with a host of one hundred thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days he held all of Longxi and commanded one hundred thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 十三年，僭帝號於蘭州，以妻鞠為後，仁杲為太子。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he usurped the imperial title at Lanzhou, made his wife Ju empress, and Rengao crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of his reign he declared himself emperor at Lanzhou, crowned his wife Ju as empress, and named Rengao crown prince.

sentences.zh: 即其先墓置陵邑，立廟城南，陳兵數萬展墓訖，大饗。

translations.literal: At his ancestors' tombs he established a mausoleum district, built a temple south of the city, arrayed tens of thousands of troops to open the graves, and held a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his family's ancestral graves into an imperial burial ground, erected a temple south of the city, paraded tens of thousands of soldiers through the tomb rites, and held a lavish banquet.

sentences.zh: 使仁杲圍秦州；

translations.literal: He sent Rengao to besiege Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rengao to lay siege to Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 仁越趨劍口，掠河池，太守蕭瑀拒卻之。

translations.literal: Renyue pressed toward Jiankou, raided Hechi, and the prefect Xiao Yu repulsed him.
translations.idiomatic: Renyue drove toward Jiankou and plundered Hechi, but the prefect Xiao Yu beat him back.

sentences.zh: 遣將常仲興度河擊李軌，與軌將李赟戰昌松，仲興敗，軍沒於軌。

translations.literal: He dispatched the general Chang Zhongxing to cross the river and attack Li Gui; at Changsong he fought Li Gui's general Li Yun, Zhongxing was defeated, and the army was lost to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chang Zhongxing across the river against Li Gui. At Changsong, Zhongxing met Li Gui's commander Li Yun, was defeated, and his entire force was swallowed up.

sentences.zh: 仁杲克秦州，舉往都之。

translations.literal: Rengao captured Qinzhou, and Ju moved his capital there.
translations.idiomatic: When Rengao took Qinzhou, Xue Ju shifted his seat of power to that city.

sentences.zh: 仁杲寇扶風，汧源賊唐弼拒，不得進。

translations.literal: Rengao raided Fufeng; the Qianyuan bandit Tang Bi resisted, and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao marched against Fufeng, but the outlaw Tang Bi of Qianyuan blocked him and he could not break through.

sentences.zh: 初，弼立李弘芝為天子，有眾十萬。

translations.literal: Earlier Bi had installed Li Hongzhi as Son of Heaven and commanded a host of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bi had earlier set up Li Hongzhi as emperor and commanded a force of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 舉遣使招弼，弼殺弘芝從舉。

translations.literal: Ju sent envoys to win Bi over; Bi killed Hongzhi and joined Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju sent envoys to recruit him. Tang Bi killed Hongzhi and threw in his lot with Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 仁杲間弼無備，襲之，盡奪其眾，弼以數百騎走。

translations.literal: Rengao, finding Bi off guard, raided him, seized all his troops, and Bi fled with only a few hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao caught Tang Bi unprepared, struck by surprise, and absorbed his entire army. Tang Bi escaped with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 軍益張，號二十萬。

translations.literal: The army grew still greater, claiming two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His forces swelled further until he claimed two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 將窺京師。

translations.literal: He was about to menace the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared to threaten the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 會高祖入關，遂留攻扶風，秦王擊破之，斬首數千級，逐北至隴還。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the passes, Ju lingered to attack Fufeng; the Prince of Qin routed him, took several thousand heads, pursued him north to Long, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu entered the Guanzhong region, Xue Ju stayed to besiege Fufeng. The Prince of Qin shattered his army, took several thousand heads, chased him north to the Long Mountains, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 舉畏王，遂逾隴走，問其下曰：「古有降天子乎？」

translations.literal: Ju feared the Prince and fled west over Long, asking his followers, "In antiquity has there been one who submitted to a Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the Prince of Qin, Xue Ju fled back across the Long Mountains and asked his officers, "Has anyone in history ever surrendered to a Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 偽黃門侍郎褚亮曰：「昔趙佗以南粵歸漢，蜀劉禪亦仕晉，近世蕭琮，其家今存，轉禍為福，嘗有之。」

translations.literal: The false Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary Chu Liang said, "Formerly Zhao Tuo brought Southern Yue to Han; Liu Shan of Shu also served Jin; in recent times Xiao Cong—his house still endures. Turning calamity into fortune has indeed happened before."
translations.idiomatic: The pretender's chamberlain Chu Liang answered, "Zhao Tuo once brought the Southern Yue into Han submission. Liu Shan of Shu served the Jin. In our own day Xiao Cong submitted, and his line still stands. Turning disaster into blessing has happened before."

sentences.zh: 衛尉卿郝瑗曰：「亮之言非也。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Guards Hao Yuan said, "Liang's words are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Guards Hao Yuan said, "Liang is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖兵屢敗，蜀先主嘗亡其妻子。

translations.literal: Formerly Han's Founding Emperor's armies were repeatedly defeated; the Former Lord of Shu once lost wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor of Han lost battle after battle. The Former Lord of Shu once lost his wife and children in defeat.

sentences.zh: 夫戰固有勝負，豈可一不勝便為亡國計乎？」

translations.literal: In war there are naturally victories and defeats—how can one defeat be grounds for plotting the ruin of a state?"
translations.idiomatic: War brings victory and defeat by nature. How can a single loss be reason to plan for national extinction?"

sentences.zh: 舉亦悔其言，乃曰：「聊試公等。」

translations.literal: Ju also regretted his own words and said, "I was merely testing you all."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju regretted having asked and said, "I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: 即厚賜瑗，以為謀主。

translations.literal: He at once richly rewarded Yuan and made him his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Hao Yuan lavishly on the spot and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 瑗請連梁師都，厚賂突厥，合從東向。

translations.literal: Yuan urged alliance with Liang Shidu, lavish bribes to the Turks, and a joint advance eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan urged an alliance with Liang Shidu, heavy bribes to the Turks, and a combined drive eastward.

sentences.zh: 舉從之，約突厥莫賀咄設犯京師。

translations.literal: Ju agreed and arranged for the Turkic Moheduo she to invade the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju agreed and arranged for the Turkic Moheduo she to strike at the capital.

sentences.zh: 會都水監宇文歆使突厥，歆說止其兵，故舉謀塞。

translations.literal: When the Director of Waterways Yuwen Xin was sent on mission to the Turks, Xin persuaded them to halt their troops, and Ju's scheme was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xin, Director of Waterways, was sent on embassy to the Turks and talked them out of marching. Xue Ju's plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 仁杲多力善騎射，軍中號萬人敵，性賊悍。

translations.literal: Rengao was powerful, skilled at mounted archery, called in the army a match for ten thousand, and by nature cruel and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao was immensely strong, a superb mounted archer, hailed in camp as a match for ten thousand men, and by nature savage and brutal.

sentences.zh: 初，舉每破陣，軍獲俘，仁杲必斷舌刈鼻，或舂斮之。

translations.literal: From the first, whenever Ju broke an enemy line and the army took prisoners, Rengao would cut out tongues and slice off noses, or pound them in mortars.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xue Ju won a battle and prisoners were taken, Rengao would cut out their tongues, slice off their noses, or pound them to pieces in mortars.

sentences.zh: 其妻亦兇暴，喜鞭楚人，見不勝痛宛轉於地者，則埋其足，露腹背受棰。

translations.literal: His wife was likewise ferocious, delighting in flogging people; when she saw one who could not bear the pain writhing on the ground, she would bury his feet and expose belly and back to the rod.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was equally vicious and loved to flog captives. If a victim writhed on the ground from the pain, she had his feet buried in the earth so that only his belly and back were exposed for the beating.

sentences.zh: 人畏而不親。

translations.literal: People feared them and did not draw close.
translations.idiomatic: Men feared them and would not rally to their cause.

sentences.zh: 仁杲多殺人，淫略民人妻妾。

translations.literal: Rengao killed many and violated the wives and concubines of common people.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao killed freely and seized the wives and concubines of the populace.

sentences.zh: 嘗得庾信子立，怒其不降，礫之火，漸割以啖士。

translations.literal: Once he captured Yu Xin's son Li, and enraged that he would not submit, stoned him and burned him, gradually slicing the flesh to feed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He once captured Li, son of the poet Yu Xin. Furious that Li would not submit, he had him stoned and burned alive, then carved the flesh piece by piece to feed his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 拔秦州，取富人倒懸，以酢註鼻，或杙其隱，以求財。

translations.literal: After taking Qinzhou he seized the wealthy, hung them upside down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, or drove stakes into their privates to extort wealth.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Qinzhou he took wealthy men, hung them head down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, or drove stakes into their groins to wring out their fortunes.

sentences.zh: 雖舉殘猛，亦惡之，每戒曰：「汝材略足辦事，而傷於虐，終覆吾宗。」

translations.literal: Though Ju himself was cruel and fierce, he also detested this and often warned him, "Your talent and plans are enough to get things done, but your cruelty will in the end destroy our house."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xue Ju was himself ruthless, he loathed his son's excesses and often warned him, "Your abilities are enough to win wars, but your cruelty will destroy our house in the end."

sentences.zh: 及繼立，與諸將素有隙者，鹹猜懼。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to power, all generals who had long borne grudges against him alike grew suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Rengao took power, every commander who had old grievances against him grew suspicious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 郝瑗哭舉，病不起，繇是兵稍衰。

translations.literal: Hao Yuan wept for Ju, fell ill and could not rise; from this the army gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yuan mourned Xue Ju until he fell ill and could not leave his bed, and from that point the army's strength began to ebb.

sentences.zh: 秦王率諸將復壁高墌，諸將請戰，王曰：「我軍新恤，銳氣少；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin led the generals to entrench again at Gaoping; the generals asked to give battle, and the Prince said, "Our army has newly mourned and lacks keen edge;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin led his commanders back to fortify at Gaoping. When they asked to fight, he said, "Our army is still in mourning and lacks its fighting edge;

sentences.zh: 賊驟勝而驕，有輕我心。

translations.literal: the rebels have won suddenly and grown arrogant—they hold us in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy has won too quickly and grown arrogant. They underestimate us.

sentences.zh: 我閉壁以折之，伺衰而擊，可一戰禽也。」

translations.literal: If we shut our walls to break their spirit and strike when they weaken, we can take them in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: If we hold our walls to break their spirit and strike when they falter, we can destroy them in one battle."

sentences.zh: 因令軍中曰：「敢言戰者斬！」

translations.literal: He then ordered the army, "Whoever speaks of giving battle shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed through the camp, "Anyone who urges battle will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 久之，仁杲糧乏，挑戰，不許。

translations.literal: After a long while Rengao's grain ran short; he offered challenge, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Rengao's supplies ran out. He taunted them to fight, but they would not come out.

sentences.zh: 其將牟君才、內史令翟長愻以眾降，左僕射鐘俱仇以河州降。

translations.literal: His generals Mou Juncai and the Palace Secretary Zhai Changsun surrendered with their troops; the Left Vice Minister Zhong Juqiu surrendered Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Mou Juncai and Palace Secretary Zhai Changsun came over with their men. Left Vice Minister Zhong Juqiu surrendered Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 王策賊可破，遣將軍龐玉擊宗羅睺於淺水原，戰酣，王以勁兵扌壽其背，羅睺敗，王率騎追奔，於是悉軍馳之，曰：「勢破竹，不可失也。」

translations.literal: The Prince judged the rebels could be broken, sent General Pang Yu to strike Zong Luohou at Qianshuiyuan; when the battle grew fierce the Prince hit his rear with crack troops; Luohou was defeated; the Prince led cavalry in pursuit, then drove the whole army forward, saying, "The momentum splits bamboo—we must not let it slip."
translations.idiomatic: Judging the enemy ripe for defeat, the Prince sent General Pang Yu against Zong Luohou at Qianshui Plain. When the fight was hottest he hit Luohou from the rear with his best troops. Luohou broke, and the Prince led the cavalry in pursuit, then hurled the whole army forward, crying, "The momentum splits bamboo—we must not let this chance slip."

sentences.zh: 夜半，至析墌；

translations.literal: At midnight they reached Xizhi;
translations.idiomatic: By midnight they reached Xizhi;

sentences.zh: 遲明，圍合。

translations.literal: at dawn the encirclement closed.
translations.idiomatic: at first light the ring of siege closed tight.

sentences.zh: 仁杲率偽官屬降，王受之，以仁杲歸京師，及酋黨數十人皆斬之。

translations.literal: Rengao led the false officials to surrender; the Prince accepted it, sent Rengao to the capital, and beheaded him together with several tens of chieftains and partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Rengao led his pretender court in surrender. The Prince accepted it, sent Rengao to the capital, and executed him along with several dozen of his chieftains and followers.

sentences.zh: 舉父子盜隴西五年滅。

translations.literal: The father and son Ju had ravaged Longxi for five years before perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son had held Longxi as rebels for five years before they were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 初，仁杲降，諸將賀，且問曰：「羅睺雖破，而賊城尚堅，王能下之，何也？」

translations.literal: When Rengao first surrendered, the generals congratulated him and also asked, "Though Luohou was broken, the rebel city was still strong—how could Your Highness take it?"
translations.idiomatic: When Rengao first surrendered, the commanders congratulated the Prince and asked, "Luohou was beaten, but the rebel stronghold was still formidable. How did Your Highness bring it down so quickly?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「羅睺健將，非急追之，使得還城，未可取也。

translations.literal: The Prince said, "Luohou is a stalwart commander—unless pursued hotly, if he were allowed to return to the city it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Luohou is a formidable commander. Unless we pursued him hard and kept him from regaining the city, we could never have taken it.

sentences.zh: 故吾使賊不及計，是以克之。」

translations.literal: Therefore I kept the rebels from regrouping—that is why we conquered it."
translations.idiomatic: I gave the enemy no time to recover. That is why we won."

sentences.zh: 諸將咨服。

translations.literal: The generals sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders marveled at his judgment.

sentences.zh: 仁杲已敗，其將旁屳地降，詔即統其兵，未幾復叛。

translations.literal: After Rengao's defeat his general Pang Tudi surrendered; an edict at once placed him in command of his troops, but before long he rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: After Rengao's fall his general Pang Tudi submitted and was ordered to keep command of his men, but he rebelled again before long.

sentences.zh: 屳地，羌豪也，舉父子信倚之。

translations.literal: Tudi was a Qiang magnate in whom the Ju father and son had placed great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Tudi was a powerful Qiang chieftain whom father and son Xue Ju had relied on heavily.

sentences.zh: 至是入南山，繇商洛出漢川，眾數千，所過剽害，敗大將龐玉。

translations.literal: At this time he entered the Southern Mountains, came out through Shangluo into Hanchuan with several thousand men, plundered wherever he passed, and defeated the Grand General Pang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He now fled into the Southern Mountains, emerged through Shangluo into the Han River valley with several thousand followers, plundered every district he crossed, and defeated Grand General Pang Yu.

sentences.zh: 至始州，掠王氏女，醉寢於野，王取屳地所佩刀斬之，送首梁州。

translations.literal: Reaching Shizhou he seized a Wang clanswoman; drunk he slept in the open; the girl took Tudi's belt knife and cut him down, sending his head to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizhou he abducted a woman of the Wang clan. Drunk, he slept in the open country. She took the knife from his belt and killed him, then sent his head to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔封女為崇義夫人。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed the woman as Lady of Chongyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ennobled the woman as Lady of Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 李軌，字處則，涼州姑臧人。

translations.literal: Li Gui, style Chuze, was a native of Guzang in Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui, styled Chuze, came from Guzang in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 略知書，有智辯。

translations.literal: He had some knowledge of books and possessed wit in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning and a sharp mind for argument.

sentences.zh: 家以財雄邊，好赒人急，鄉黨稱之。

translations.literal: His family dominated the frontier through wealth; he delighted in relieving others in distress, and his township praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was wealthy enough to dominate the border country. He was generous to neighbors in need, and his community spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，補鷹揚府司兵。

translations.literal: During the Sui Daye era he was appointed clerk of the Yingyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served as clerk in the Yingyang Guard.

sentences.zh: 薛舉亂金城，軌與同郡曹珍、關謹、梁碩、李赟、安修仁等計曰：「舉暴悍，今其兵必來。

translations.literal: When Xue Ju rebelled at Jincheng, Gui with his fellow townsman Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others plotted, saying, "Ju is brutal and fierce—his troops will surely come.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju rose at Jincheng, Li Gui met with his countrymen Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others and said, "Xue Ju is savage and brutal. His army will come for us.

sentences.zh: 吏孱怯，無足與計者。

translations.literal: The officials are weak and timid—not worth consulting.
translations.idiomatic: The officials are weak and cowardly. They are no help at all.

sentences.zh: 欲相戮力，據河右，以觀天下變，庸能束手以妻子餌人哉？」

translations.literal: We wish to join forces, hold the lands west of the river, and watch how the realm changes—how can we fold our arms and offer wife and children as bait to others?"
translations.idiomatic: Let us join forces, hold the lands west of the Yellow River, and watch how the empire unfolds. How can we sit idle and offer our wives and children as prey to another man?"

sentences.zh: 眾允其謀，共舉兵，然莫適敢主。

translations.literal: The assembly approved the plan and together raised troops, yet none dared to take the lead.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed and took up arms together, but no one dared assume command.

sentences.zh: 曹珍曰：「我聞讖書，李氏當王。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen said, "I have heard in prophetic books that the house of Li is destined to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen said, "I have read the prophecies. The house of Li is destined to rule.

sentences.zh: 今軌賢，非天啟乎！」

translations.literal: Gui is worthy now—is this not Heaven's opening?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui is worthy. Is this not Heaven's sign?"

sentences.zh: 遂共降拜以聽命。

translations.literal: They thereupon all bowed in submission to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed low and pledged themselves to his command.

sentences.zh: 修仁夜率諸胡入內苑城，建旗大呼，軌集眾應之，執虎賁郎將謝統師、郡丞韋士政，遂自稱河西大涼王，署官屬，準開皇故事。

translations.literal: Xiuren by night led the various Hu into the Inner Garden city, raised banners and shouted; Gui gathered the host to respond, seized the Tiger Elite Commander Xie Tongshi and the prefectural aide Wei Shizheng, then styled himself Great King of Liang west of the river, appointed officials, and followed the precedents of the Kaihuang era.
translations.idiomatic: That night An Xiuren led the frontier tribes into the Inner Garden city, raised banners, and raised the cry. Li Gui rallied his followers, seized Tiger Elite Commander Xie Tongshi and prefectural aide Wei Shizheng, and proclaimed himself Great King of Liang west of the river. He appointed a full court on the model of Emperor Wen's Kaihuang reign.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥曷娑那可汗弟達度闕設內屬，保會寧川，至是稱可汗，降於軌。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turkic Tujue she, brother of Khan Ashina, had submitted and held Huiningchuan; now he styled himself khan and submitted to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic Tujue she, brother of Khan Ashina, had earlier submitted and held the Huining River valley. He now styled himself khan and came over to Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 謹等議盡殺隋官，分其產。

translations.literal: Jin and the others urged killing all Sui officials and dividing their property.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jin and others urged that all Sui officials be killed and their property divided.

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「諸公既見推，當稟吾約。

translations.literal: Gui said, "Since you gentlemen have elevated me, you should abide by my covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said, "Since you have chosen me as your leader, you must accept my terms.

sentences.zh: 今軍以義興，意在救亂，殺人取財是為賊，何以求濟乎？」

translations.literal: Our army rises in righteousness to rescue the realm from chaos—killing for wealth makes us mere bandits; how then can we seek success?"
translations.idiomatic: We raise this army in the name of righteousness to rescue the realm from chaos. Killing for profit makes us nothing but bandits. How can we hope to succeed that way?"

sentences.zh: 乃以統師為太仆卿，士政太府卿。

translations.literal: He then made Tongshi Grand Master of the Stud and Shizheng Grand Master of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Tongshi Grand Master of the Stud and Shizheng Grand Master of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 會薛舉遣兵來侵，軌遣將敗之昌松，斬首二千級，悉虜其眾，軌縱還之。

translations.literal: When Xue Ju sent troops to invade, Gui dispatched a general who defeated them at Changsong, took two thousand heads, captured the entire force, and Gui released them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju sent an army against him, Li Gui's commander defeated it at Changsong, took two thousand heads, and captured the entire force. Li Gui sent every prisoner home.

sentences.zh: 李赟曰：「今力戰而俘，又縱以資敵，不如盡坑之。」

translations.literal: Li Yun said, "We fought hard to take them captive, yet you release them to strengthen the enemy—better to bury them all alive."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun said, "We fought hard to take these men, and now you release them to strengthen the enemy. We should bury them all alive."

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Gui said, "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said, "No.

sentences.zh: 若天命歸我，當禽其主，此皆我有也；

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate is mine, we should capture their lord—these men will all be mine;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven favors us, we will capture their leader, and these men will be ours in any case;

sentences.zh: 不者，徒留何益？」

translations.literal: if not, what use is it to keep them?"
translations.idiomatic: if not, what good does it do to keep them?"

sentences.zh: 遂遣之。

translations.literal: He then sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拔張掖、燉煌、西平、枹罕，悉有河西。

translations.literal: Before long he took Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping, and Fuhan, and held all lands west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he captured Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping, and Fuhan and held the entire Hexi corridor.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，高祖方事薛舉，遣使涼州，璽書慰結，謂軌為從弟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, while Gaozu was still campaigning against Xue Ju, he sent envoys to Liangzhou with an imperial letter of comfort and alliance, calling Gui his younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, while Emperor Gaozu was still fighting Xue Ju, he sent envoys to Liangzhou with an imperial letter of friendship, addressing Li Gui as his younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 軌喜，乃遣弟懋入朝。

translations.literal: Gui rejoiced and sent his younger brother Mao to court.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Li Gui sent his younger brother Mao to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝拜懋大將軍，還之，詔鴻臚少卿張俟德持節冊拜軌涼王、涼州總管，給羽葆鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Mao Grand General and sent him back; he ordered the Vice Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Relations Zhang Side to bear credentials enfeoffing Gui as King of Liang and Area Commander of Liangzhou, granting one set of feathered canopy and martial music.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Mao a Grand General and sent him home. He ordered Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Side to invest Li Gui as King of Liang and military governor of Liangzhou, with a full set of royal insignia and martial music.

sentences.zh: 會軌僭帝號，建元安樂，以其子伯玉為太子，長史曹珍為尚書左僕射，攻陷河州。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Gui had usurped the imperial title, adopted the era name Anle, made his son Boyu crown prince and Chief Clerk Cao Zhen Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and captured Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Gui had declared himself emperor with the era name Anle, named his son Boyu crown prince, made Chief Clerk Cao Zhen Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and captured Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 俟德至，軌召其下議曰：「李氏有天下，歷運所屬，已宅京邑。

translations.literal: When Side arrived, Gui summoned his followers to discuss, saying, "The house of Li holds the realm—the cycle of fortune belongs to them; they already dwell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Side arrived, Li Gui called his advisers together and said, "The house of Li holds the Mandate. Their fortune is established, and they already rule from the capital.

sentences.zh: 一姓不可競王，今欲去帝號，東向受冊，可乎？」

translations.literal: One surname cannot compete for kingship. If I now wish to remove my imperial title and face east to receive investiture, is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: A single clan cannot vie for supremacy forever. What if I renounce my imperial title and accept investiture from the east—would that work?

sentences.zh: 曹珍曰：「隋亡，英雄焱起，號帝王者瓜分鼎峙。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen said: "When the Sui perished, heroes blazed up everywhere; those who proclaimed themselves emperors carved up the realm like a tripartite cauldron standing on its legs.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen replied, "After the Sui fell, heroes rose everywhere, and every man who claimed the title of emperor held his own piece of the realm.

sentences.zh: 唐自保關、雍，大涼奄河右，業已為天子，奈何受人官？

translations.literal: Tang secured itself in the Guan and Yong regions; Great Liang has swept across the lands west of the Yellow River. We are already emperors—how can we accept appointment from others?
translations.idiomatic: The Tang holds Guan and Yong; we of Great Liang dominate the west of the River—we are already emperors in our own right. Why should we accept offices from others?

sentences.zh: 必欲以小事大，請行蕭詧故事，稱梁帝而臣於周。」

translations.literal: If you must treat the lesser as subordinate to the greater, I ask that we follow the precedent of Xiao Cha, styling ourselves Emperors of Liang while serving Zhou as subjects."
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on playing the lesser power to their greater one, follow Xiao Cha's example—call ourselves Emperors of Liang while submitting as vassals to Zhou."

sentences.zh: 軌從之，乃遣偽尚書左丞鄧曉來朝，奉書稱「從弟大涼皇帝」。

translations.literal: Li Gui followed this advice and sent the false dynasty's Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, Deng Xiao, to court, presenting a letter addressing him as "Younger Brother, Emperor of Great Liang."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui agreed. He dispatched Deng Xiao, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing in his court, with a letter calling the Tang emperor "Younger Brother, Emperor of Great Liang."

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「軌謂朕為兄，此不臣也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said angrily: "Li Gui calls me his elder brother—this is disloyal to a subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious. "Li Gui calls me his younger brother—that is no posture of a loyal subject.

sentences.zh: 囚曉不遣。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Deng Xiao and refused to send him back.
translations.idiomatic: He had Deng Xiao imprisoned and held him there.

sentences.zh: 初，軌以梁碩為謀主，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Gui had taken Liang Shuo as his chief strategist and appointed him Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning Li Gui had relied on Liang Shuo as his chief strategist, appointing him Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 碩有算略，眾憚之，嘗見故西域胡種族盛，勸軌備之，因與戶部尚書安修仁交怨；

translations.literal: Liang Shuo was skilled in planning and strategy, and everyone feared him. He once observed that the Hu clans from the Western Regions were growing strong and urged Li Gui to guard against them; because of this he came into conflict with An Xiuren, Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo was a clever strategist whom everyone feared. When he saw Western Region Hu clans growing in strength, he warned Li Gui to prepare against them—drawing the resentment of An Xiuren, Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又軌子仲琰嘗候碩，碩不為起，仲琰憾之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Li Gui's son Zhongyan once called on Liang Shuo, and Liang Shuo did not rise to greet him; Zhongyan resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui's son Zhongyan once visited Liang Shuo, who did not rise to receive him. Zhongyan never forgot the slight.

sentences.zh: 乃相與譖碩。

translations.literal: Together they slandered Liang Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: They joined forces to slander him.

sentences.zh: 軌不察，賫鴆其家殺之，繇是故人稍疑懼，不為用。

translations.literal: Li Gui failed to see through it and sent poison wine to his home to kill him. From this their associates gradually grew suspicious and fearful, and would not serve him wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui was deceived. He sent poison wine to Liang Shuo's home and had him killed. From then on, his followers grew wary and no longer gave him their full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 有胡巫妄曰：「上帝將遣玉女從天來。」

translations.literal: A Hu shaman falsely declared: "The Lord on High will send a jade maiden down from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A Hu shaman proclaimed a vision: "The Lord on High will send a jade maiden down from heaven.

sentences.zh: 遂召兵築臺以候女，多所糜損。

translations.literal: Li Gui then called up soldiers to build a tower to await the maiden, wasting much in the process.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui mobilized troops to build a tower to await her arrival, squandering great resources in the effort.

sentences.zh: 屬薦饑，人相食，軌毀家貲賑之，不能給，議發倉粟，曹珍亦勸之。

translations.literal: Famine followed. People ate one another. Li Gui exhausted his family's wealth to relieve them but could not suffice. They debated opening the granaries, and Cao Zhen also urged this.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck; people resorted to cannibalism. Li Gui spent his family's fortune on relief but still could not meet the need. Officials debated releasing grain from the storehouses, and Cao Zhen agreed.

sentences.zh: 謝統師等故隋官，心內不附，每引結群胡排其用事臣，因是欲離沮其眾，乃廷詰珍曰：「百姓餓死皆弱不足事者，壯勇士終不肯困。

translations.literal: Xie Tongshi and others, former Sui officials, were inwardly disloyal. They constantly rallied the Hu groups to oppose Li Gui's officers in power. Wishing thereby to alienate and discourage his followers, Xie Tongshi publicly challenged Cao Zhen in court: "Those among the common people who starve to death are the weak and worthless—strong, brave men will never allow themselves to be brought to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tongshi and other former Sui officials were secretly disloyal. They constantly rallied the Hu factions against Li Gui's inner circle, hoping to sow division. In open court Xie Tongshi challenged Cao Zhen: "Those who starve are the weak and useless—no strong warrior will ever let himself be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 且儲廩以備不虞，豈宜妄散惠孱小乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, the storehouses are kept for unforeseen emergencies—how can we rashly disburse them to favor the feeble and small?
translations.idiomatic: And the granaries are kept against emergencies—why waste them on the helpless and weak?

sentences.zh: 僕射茍附下，非國計。」

translations.literal: The Vice Director curries favor with Your Majesty—this is not a policy for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director is merely flattering you—that is no sound policy for the realm.

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Li Gui said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 乃閉粟。

translations.literal: He then closed the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The granaries were shut.

sentences.zh: 下益怨，多欲叛去。

translations.literal: The common people grew ever more resentful, and many wished to rebel and leave.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment deepened below, and many wanted to rebel and flee.

sentences.zh: 會修仁兄興貴本在長安，自表詣涼州招軌。

translations.literal: It happened that An Xiuren's elder brother Xinggui was in Chang'an and volunteered to go to Liangzhou to win Li Gui over.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened, An Xiuren's elder brother An Xinggui was in Chang'an. He volunteered to go to Liangzhou and persuade Li Gui to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「軌據河西，連吐谷渾、突厥，今興兵討擊尚為難，單使弄頰可下邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Li Gui holds the Hexi region and is allied with Tuyuhun and the Turks. Even raising troops to attack would still be difficult—can a lone envoy wagging his cheeks bring him down?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Li Gui holds Hexi and is allied with Tuyuhun and the Turks. Even a full military campaign would be difficult—can a lone envoy talking him into surrender really succeed?

sentences.zh: 興貴曰：「軌盛強誠然，若曉以逆順禍福，宜聽。

translations.literal: Xinggui said: "It is true that Li Gui is strong and formidable. If one explains to him the right and wrong of loyalty and rebellion and the blessings and calamities that follow, he ought to listen.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui replied, "Li Gui is indeed formidable. But if we explain to him the consequences of loyalty versus rebellion, he may listen.

sentences.zh: 如憑固不受，臣世涼州豪望，多識其士民，而修仁為軌信任，典事樞者數十人，若候隙圖之，無不濟。」

translations.literal: If he stubbornly refuses, I am a prominent figure in Liangzhou by birth and know many of its gentry and common people. Xiuren is trusted by Li Gui, and several dozen men hold key posts in his administration. If we wait for an opening and plot accordingly, nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: If he holds out, I am a native magnate of Liangzhou and know its people well. Xiuren enjoys Li Gui's trust, and dozens of men hold key positions. Find the right moment, and we can bring him down.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 興貴至涼州，軌授以左右衛大將軍，因間訪興貴以自安策。

translations.literal: When Xinggui reached Liangzhou, Li Gui appointed him General of the Left and Right Guard and privately asked him for advice on how to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: When An Xinggui arrived in Liangzhou, Li Gui made him General of the Left and Right Guard and asked him privately how best to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 興貴對曰：「涼州僻遠，財力雕耗，雖勝兵十萬，而地不過千里，無險固自守。

translations.literal: Xinggui replied: "Liangzhou is remote and isolated; its wealth and strength are exhausted. Although you have a hundred thousand fit soldiers, your territory does not exceed a thousand li, and there are no strong natural defenses to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui answered, "Liangzhou is remote and exhausted. You may field a hundred thousand men, but your territory spans barely a thousand li, with no natural defenses to speak of.

sentences.zh: 又濱接戎狄，戎狄，豺狼也，非我族類。

translations.literal: Furthermore it borders the Rong and Di—those barbarians are wolves and not of our kind.
translations.idiomatic: And it borders the barbarians of the frontier—wolves, not kin.

sentences.zh: 今唐家據京師，略定中原，攻必下，戰必勝，蓋天啟也。

translations.literal: Now the House of Tang holds the capital, has largely pacified the Central Plains, and wherever it attacks it prevails, wherever it fights it wins—surely this is Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang holds the capital and is pacifying the heartland. Where they attack, they conquer; where they fight, they win. Heaven itself favors them.

sentences.zh: 若舉河西地奉圖東歸，雖漢竇融未足吾比。」

translations.literal: If you offer up the lands of Hexi with maps and charts and go east to submit, even Han dynasty's Dou Rong would not compare to you.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender Hexi with maps and tribute in hand, and your reward would surpass even Dou Rong of the Han.

sentences.zh: 軌默不答，久之，曰：「昔吳王濞以江左兵猶稱己為東帝，我今舉河右，不得為西帝乎？

translations.literal: Li Gui was silent and did not reply. After a long while he said: "In former times King Liu Bi of Wu, with troops from the lands east of the Yangtze, still called himself Eastern Emperor. I now hold the lands west of the Yellow River—may I not be Western Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui was silent for a long time. Then he said, "Liu Bi held only the lower Yangtze and still styled himself Eastern Emperor. I hold the west of the River—why should I not be Western Emperor?

sentences.zh: 雖唐強大，如我何？

translations.literal: However powerful Tang may be, what can it do to me?
translations.idiomatic: However powerful the Tang may be, what can they do to me?

sentences.zh: 君無為唐誘致我。」

translations.literal: Do not try to lure me on behalf of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Do not try to lure me into Tang's net.

sentences.zh: 興貴懼，謝曰：「竊聞富貴不居故鄉，如衣錦夜行。

translations.literal: Xinggui was afraid and apologized: "I have heard it said that one who attains wealth and rank does not stay in his old home, just as one who wears brocade does not walk at night.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui was afraid. "Forgive me," he said. "They say a man does not wear his glory in his hometown—it is like parading brocade in the dark.

sentences.zh: 今合宗蒙任，敢有它誌！」

translations.literal: Now my entire clan has received appointment—how would I dare have other designs!
translations.idiomatic: My whole clan has been favored with office—how could I harbor any other intent?

sentences.zh: 興貴知軌不可以說，乃與脩仁等潛引諸胡兵圍其城，軌以步騎千余出戰。

translations.literal: Xinggui knew Li Gui could not be persuaded. He then secretly joined with Xiuren and others to bring in Hu soldiers to surround the city. Li Gui led more than a thousand infantry and cavalry out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing Li Gui could not be persuaded, An Xinggui secretly joined Xiuren and others to rally Hu troops against the city. Li Gui marched out with more than a thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 先是，薛舉柱國奚道宜率羌兵奔軌，軌許以刺史而不與，道宜怨，故共擊軌。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi Daoyi, a pillar-general under Xue Ju, had led Qiang troops to join Li Gui. Li Gui promised him the post of regional inspector but did not grant it. Daoyi bore a grudge and therefore joined in the attack on Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi Daoyi, a general under Xue Ju, had brought Qiang troops to Li Gui's side. Li Gui had promised him a prefecture but never delivered. Resentful, Daoyi now joined the assault.

sentences.zh: 軌敗入城，引兵登陴，須外援。

translations.literal: Li Gui was defeated and retreated into the city, leading his troops onto the battlements, awaiting outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Li Gui retreated behind the walls and manned the ramparts, waiting for help from outside.

sentences.zh: 興貴傳言曰：「唐使我來取軌，不從者罪三族。」

translations.literal: Xinggui sent word around: "Tang sent me to seize Li Gui. Whoever does not comply will have three generations punished.
translations.idiomatic: An Xinggui spread the word: "The Tang sent me to take Li Gui. Defy me, and three generations of your family will pay.

sentences.zh: 於是諸城不敢動。

translations.literal: Thereupon none of the cities dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: None of the surrounding cities dared move.

sentences.zh: 軌嘆曰：「人心去矣，天亡我乎？」

translations.literal: Li Gui sighed: "The people's hearts have departed—does Heaven mean to destroy me?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui sighed. "Heaven has taken the people's hearts from me—is this my end?

sentences.zh: 攜妻子上玉女臺，屬酒為別。

translations.literal: He took his wife and children up to the Jade Maiden Tower and entrusted wine for a farewell.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the Jade Maiden Tower with his wife and children and shared a final cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 脩仁執送之，斬於長安。

translations.literal: Xiuren seized him and sent him away; he was executed in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren seized him and sent him to Chang'an, where he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 自起至亡凡三年。

translations.literal: From his rise to his fall was altogether three years.
translations.idiomatic: From rise to fall, his regime lasted three years.

sentences.zh: 詔興貴為右武候大將軍，封涼國公，賜帛萬段；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xinggui General of the Right Martial Guard, enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang, and bestowed ten thousand lengths of silk;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made An Xinggui General of the Right Martial Guard, Duke of Liang, with ten thousand lengths of silk;

sentences.zh: 修仁左武候大將軍，申國公，並給田宅，封六百戶。

translations.literal: Xiuren was made General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Shen, and both were granted lands and residences with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren became General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Shen; both were granted estates and fiefs of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時鄧曉聞軌敗，入賀帝。

translations.literal: At that time Deng Xiao, hearing of Li Gui's defeat, entered to congratulate the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Xiao heard of Li Gui's defeat, he came to congratulate the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「而委質李軌，以使來，聞其亡，不少戚，乃蹈抃以悅我。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You pledged yourself to Li Gui and came here as his envoy. When you heard of his downfall you showed no grief, but instead stamped and clapped your hands to please me.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You pledged yourself to Li Gui and came as his envoy. When he fell, you showed no grief—you stamped and clapped to please me.

sentences.zh: 不盡心於軌，能竭節於我乎？」

translations.literal: Since you were not wholehearted toward Li Gui, can you be loyal to me?
translations.idiomatic: If you gave Li Gui so little loyalty, how can I trust yours?

sentences.zh: 遂廢不齒。

translations.literal: He was therefore dismissed and not reckoned among the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and never again counted among the court's men of standing.

sentences.zh: 劉武周，瀛州景城人。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou was a native of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou came from Jingcheng in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父匡，徙馬邑。

translations.literal: His father Liu Kuang moved to Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Kuang had moved the family to Mayi.

sentences.zh: 母趙嘗夜坐廷中，見若雄雞，光燭地，飛投其懷，起振衣，無有，感而娠，生武周。

translations.literal: His mother Zhao was once sitting in the courtyard at night when she saw what seemed to be a rooster, its light illuminating the ground. It flew into her bosom. When she rose and shook out her robe, nothing was there. Moved by this, she conceived and bore Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: One night his mother Zhao was sitting in the courtyard when she saw what looked like a rooster, radiant enough to light the ground. It flew into her bosom; when she rose and shook her robe, nothing was there. Stirred by the omen, she conceived and bore Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武周為人驍悍，善騎射，喜交豪傑。

translations.literal: Wuzhou was by nature fierce and bold, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and fond of associating with bold spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou was fierce and bold, an excellent horseman and archer who loved the company of men of spirit.

sentences.zh: 兄山伯嘗詈辱之曰：「汝不擇所與，必滅吾宗！」

translations.literal: His elder brother Shanbo once reviled and humiliated him, saying: "You do not choose your companions—we will surely be destroyed as a clan!
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shanbo once berated him: "You keep the worst company—you will bring ruin on our whole clan!

sentences.zh: 武周因去至洛，為太仆楊義臣帳下。

translations.literal: Wuzhou therefore left and went to Luoyang, serving under the Grand Minister of Studs Yang Yichen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou left home for Luoyang, where he served under Yang Yichen, Grand Minister of Studs.

sentences.zh: 募征遼，有功，補建節校尉。

translations.literal: Recruited for the Liaodong campaign, he performed meritorious service and was appointed a Jianjie Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered for the Liaodong campaign, distinguished himself, and was made a Jianjie Commandant.

sentences.zh: 還馬邑，為鷹揚府校尉。

translations.literal: Returning to Mayi, he became a commandant in the Eagle-Flying Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Mayi, he was appointed commandant of the Eagle-Flying Guard.

sentences.zh: 太守王仁恭以其州裏雄，頗愛遇之，令總虞候，直閤下。

translations.literal: The prefect Wang Rengong, because he was a local hero in the prefecture, treated him with considerable favor and put him in charge of the patrol guards, stationed below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Rengong, recognizing him as a local strongman, favored him and put him in charge of the guard patrols at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 久之，盜仁恭侍兒，懼覺誅，又見天下已亂，陰有異計，因宣言於眾曰：「今歲饑，死者骨相枕於野，府君閉倉不恤，豈憂百姓意乎？」

translations.literal: After a long while, he stole Wang Rengong's concubine. Fearing discovery and execution, and seeing that the world was already in turmoil, he secretly formed other plans. He therefore proclaimed to the crowd: "This year there is famine, and the dead lie bone against bone in the fields. The lord of the prefecture keeps the granaries closed and shows no concern—is this the mind of one who cares for the people?
translations.idiomatic: In time he seduced Wang Rengong's concubine. Fearing exposure and execution, and seeing the realm in chaos, he secretly began plotting rebellion. He stirred the troops: "Famine has left the dead piled in the fields, while the Prefect keeps the granaries shut—is this a man who cares for his people?

sentences.zh: 以市怒其軍，皆憤怨。

translations.literal: By this he sought to provoke the army's anger; all were indignant.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to inflame the garrison—and inflame them he did.

sentences.zh: 武周知人已搖，因稱疾臥家，豪桀往候謁，遂椎牛縱酒大言曰：「盜賊方起，眾又饑，壯士守分，死溝壑。

translations.literal: Wuzhou knew the men were wavering. He therefore claimed illness and stayed at home. Bold spirits came to call on him. He slaughtered cattle, poured wine freely, and spoke boldly: "Bandits are rising everywhere, the people are starving, and if strong men keep to their station they will die in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing the troops were ready to turn, Liu Wuzhou feigned illness and received local strongmen at his home. He slaughtered an ox, poured wine freely, and declared: "Rebels are rising everywhere; famine stalks the land. A strong man who plays by the rules will die in a ditch.

sentences.zh: 今官粟紅腐於倉，誰能與我共取之？」

translations.literal: Now official grain rots red in the storehouses—who will join me in taking it?
translations.idiomatic: Official grain rots in the warehouses—who will help me take it?

sentences.zh: 諸惡少年皆願從。

translations.literal: All the unruly young men were willing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The disaffected young men of the district rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 隋大業十三年，與其徒張萬歲等十余人候仁恭視事，武周上謁，萬歲自後入斬仁恭，持首出徇，郡中無敢動者。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daye of Sui, he and more than ten of his followers including Zhang Wansui waited until Rengong was holding court. Wuzhou went forward to pay his respects; Wansui entered from behind and beheaded Rengong. Carrying the head he went out to display it, and none in the commandery dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Daye 13, Liu Wuzhou and more than a dozen followers including Zhang Wansui ambushed Wang Rengong at court. Wuzhou approached to pay respects while Wansui struck from behind and beheaded the Prefect. Wansui paraded the head through the city; no one dared move.

sentences.zh: 遂開倉賑窮絕，馳檄屬城，皆下，得兵萬余，自稱太守，遣使附突厥。

translations.literal: He then opened the granaries to relieve the destitute, sent urgent dispatches to the subordinate cities, and all submitted. He gathered more than ten thousand troops, styled himself prefect, and sent envoys to submit to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the granaries to feed the starving, sent summons to every subordinate city—all submitted. He raised more than ten thousand men, declared himself Prefect, and sent envoys to ally with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 雁門丞陳孝意、虎賁郎將王智辯合兵圍其桑乾鎮，會突闕至，武周與共擊智辯，破之，孝意奔還雁門，雁門人殺之，以城歸武周。

translations.literal: Chen Xiaoyi, assistant prefect of Yanmen, and Colonel of the Tiger Guards Wang Zhibian combined forces to besiege his Sanggan garrison. Tujue arrived, and Wuzhou joined him in attacking Zhibian and defeated him. Xiaoyi fled back to Yanmen; the people of Yanmen killed him and surrendered the city to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoyi, deputy magistrate of Yanmen, and Wang Zhibian, a Tiger Guard colonel, jointly besieged his garrison at Sanggan. When the Turks arrived, Liu Wuzhou joined them and crushed Wang Zhibian. Chen Xiaoyi fled to Yanmen, where the townspeople killed him and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 武周因襲破樓煩，進據汾陽宮，取宮人賂突厥，始畢可汗報以馬，其眾遂大，攻得定襄。

translations.literal: Wuzhou then raided and defeated Loufan, advanced to occupy Fenyang Palace, took palace women to bribe the Turks, and Shibi Khan responded with horses. His forces thus grew great, and he captured Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou smashed Loufan, seized Fenyang Palace, and sent palace women as tribute to the Turks. Khan Shibi sent horses in return; his army swelled, and he took Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 突厥以狼頭纛立武周為定楊可汗，僭稱皇帝，以妻沮為後，建元天興，衛士楊伏念為左僕射，妹婿苑君璋為內史令。

translations.literal: The Turks raised a wolf-head banner and established Wuzhou as Khan Dingyang. He usurped the title of emperor, made his wife Ju empress, established the era name Tianxing, appointed Guard Officer Yang Funian Left Vice Director, and his sister's husband Yuan Junzhang Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks invested him as Khan Dingyang beneath a wolf-head banner. He declared himself emperor, made his wife Ju empress, and adopted the era name Tianxing. Yang Funian became Left Vice Director; his brother-in-law Yuan Junzhang, Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 初，上谷賊宋金剛有眾萬余，與魏刀兒連和。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bandit leader Song Jingang of Shanggu had a force of more than ten thousand men and allied with Wei Dao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the rebel Song Jingang of Shanggu commanded more than ten thousand men and had allied with Wei Dao'er.

sentences.zh: 刀兒為竇建德所攻，金剛救之，大敗，率余眾四千保西山。

translations.literal: Dao'er was attacked by Dou Jiande. Jingang went to rescue him but was badly defeated and led his remaining four thousand troops to hold Mount Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande attacked Wei Dao'er, Song Jingang marched to his aid but suffered a crushing defeat. He retreated with four thousand survivors to hold Mount Xi.

sentences.zh: 建德招之，金剛恚曰：』建德殺魏王，吾義不往，諸君可以吾首取富貴。」

translations.literal: Jiande summoned him. Jingang said angrily: "Jiande killed the King of Wei—I, on principle, will not go to him. You gentlemen may take my head and win wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande tried to recruit him. Song Jingang refused in fury: "Jiande killed Wei Dao'er—I will not join him. Take my head and sell it for your reward, if you like.

sentences.zh: 乃拔刀，將自刎，眾抱之泣，遂與皆歸武周。

translations.literal: He then drew his sword and was about to kill himself. The crowd embraced him weeping, and together they all went over to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword to kill himself. His men threw their arms around him, weeping—and together they all defected to Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 武擊素聞金剛善兵，得之喜，封為宋王，屬以軍，分家貲半遺之。

translations.literal: Wuzhou had long heard that Jingang was skilled in warfare. Delighted to obtain him, he enfeoffed him as King of Song, entrusted him with troops, and gave him half of his household wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou had long known Song Jingang's reputation as a commander. Delighted, he made him King of Song, gave him an army, and shared half his household fortune.

sentences.zh: 金剛亦自結，出其妻而騁武周妹，說武周取晉陽，南向爭天下。

translations.literal: Jingang also pledged himself in return, sent away his wife and married Wuzhou's sister, and urged Wuzhou to seize Jinyang and turn south to contend for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang sealed the alliance by setting aside his wife and marrying Liu Wuzhou's sister. He urged Wuzhou to take Jinyang and march south to contest the empire.

sentences.zh: 武周授金剛西南道大行臺。

translations.literal: Wuzhou appointed Jingang Grand Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou appointed him Grand Commissioner for the Southwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，總兵二萬入寇，次黃蛇鎮，又連突厥，鋒無前，遂破榆次，拔介州，進圍太原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, he mustered twenty thousand troops and invaded, halting at Huangshe garrison. Joined again with the Turks, his vanguard was unstoppable. He then defeated Yuci, captured Jiezhou, and advanced to besiege Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2, he invaded with twenty thousand men and camped at Huangshe. Allied again with the Turks, his vanguard swept all before it—breaking Yuci, taking Jiezhou, and laying siege to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔遣太常少卿李仲文禦之，為賊所執，舉軍沒，仲文逃還。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Vice Minister of Ceremonies Li Zhongwen to resist him. He was captured by the rebels; the whole army was lost. Zhongwen fled back.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Vice Minister Li Zhongwen to meet him. The rebels captured Zhongwen and wiped out his army; Li escaped alone.

sentences.zh: 賊因破平遙，取石州，殺刺史王儉，略浩州。

translations.literal: The rebels then broke Pingyao, took Shizhou, killed Prefect Wang Jian, and plundered Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took Pingyao, seized Shizhou, killed Prefect Wang Jian, and raided Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔右僕射裴寂為晉州道行軍總管拒之，寂戰敗績。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Right Vice Director Pei Ji Commander-in-Chief of the Jinzhou Circuit to resist them. Ji was badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, Right Vice Director, was dispatched as Commander-in-Chief of the Jinzhou expedition—and suffered a devastating defeat.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉委并州遁，武周入據之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yuanji abandoned Bingzhou and fled. Wuzhou entered and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Yuanji abandoned Bingzhou and fled; Liu Wuzhou marched in and took it.

sentences.zh: 遣金剛攻陷晉州，執右驍衛將軍劉弘基，進破澮州。

translations.literal: He sent Jingang to capture Jinzhou, seized Right Brave Guard General Liu Hongji, and advanced to defeat Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Song Jingang to take Jinzhou, captured General Liu Hongji, and pushed on to crush Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏縣人呂崇茂殺其令，自號魏王以應賊。

translations.literal: Lü Chongmao of Xia County killed the magistrate, styled himself King of Wei, and joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In Xia County, Lü Chongmao killed the magistrate, declared himself King of Wei, and rallied to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 隋河東守將王行本與武周合。

translations.literal: Wang Xingben, a Sui garrison commander of Hedong, joined with Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingben, a Sui commander in Hedong, allied with Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 關中震動。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong trembled.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔秦王督兵進討，屯柏壁。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to supervise troops and advance to attack, encamping at Baiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to take the field; he encamped at Baiyu.

sentences.zh: 又詔永安王孝基與於筠、獨孤懷恩、唐儉等攻夏縣，不克，軍城南。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, together with Yu Yun, Dugu Huai'en, Tang Jian, and others to attack Xia County. They did not succeed and encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Yu Yun, Dugu Huai'en, and Tang Jian were sent against Xia County but failed to take it, and camped south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 崇茂與賊將尉遲敬德襲破孝基軍，四將被執。

translations.literal: Chongmao and the rebel general Yuchi Jingde raided and broke Xiaoji's army. The four generals were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chongmao and the rebel general Yuchi Jingde routed Xiaoji's force and captured all four Tang commanders.

sentences.zh: 敬德還澮州，王邀戰，破之於美良川。

translations.literal: Jingde returned to Huizhou. The Prince of Qin challenged him to battle and defeated him at Meiliangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde withdrew to Huizhou. The Prince of Qin gave battle and crushed him at Meiliangchuan.

sentences.zh: 敬德復與別帥尋相援王行本於蒲，王又破卻其軍，蒲州降。

translations.literal: Jingde again joined the separate commander Xun Xiang to aid Wang Xingben at Pu. The Prince defeated and repelled their army, and Puzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde joined Xun Xiang to relieve Wang Xingben at Pu. The Prince routed them again, and Puzhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝幸蒲津關，王自柏壁輕騎謁行在，金剛遂圍絳州。

translations.literal: The Emperor traveled to Pu Pass. The Prince rode light cavalry from Baiyu to visit the imperial quarters. Jingang thereupon besieged Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went to Pu Pass. The Prince rode light cavalry from Baiyu to report in person. Song Jingang seized the moment to besiege Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王還屯，金剛引退。

translations.literal: The Prince returned to his encampment, and Jingang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince returned to camp; Song Jingang pulled back.

sentences.zh: 武周攻李仲文於浩州，不勝。

translations.literal: Wuzhou attacked Li Zhongwen at Haozhou but did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou attacked Li Zhongwen at Haozhou but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 遣將黃子英護饟道，驃騎大將軍張德政襲斬之，虜其眾，武周部將稍離。

translations.literal: He sent General Huang Ziying to protect the supply route. General of Advance Cavalry Zhang Dezheng raided and beheaded him, captured his troops, and Wuzhou's subordinate generals gradually departed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou sent Huang Ziying to escort his supply lines. General Zhang Dezheng ambushed and killed him, captured his force, and Wuzhou's subordinates began to peel away.

sentences.zh: 金剛以糧道乏卒饑引去，王追至雀鼠谷，日中八戰，賊皆敗，斬級數萬，護輜重千乘。

translations.literal: Jingang, because the supply route was cut off and his soldiers were famished, withdrew. The Prince pursued him to Queshu Valley. Between dawn and noon there were eight battles; the rebels were defeated in all. Tens of thousands were beheaded, and a thousand supply wagons were secured.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from supplies and starving, Song Jingang retreated. The Prince chased him to Queshu Valley and fought eight battles between dawn and noon—crushing the rebels, slaying tens of thousands, and seizing a thousand supply wagons.

sentences.zh: 金剛走介州，官軍迫之，以余眾二萬出西門，背城陣，亙七里。

translations.literal: Jingang fled to Jiezhou. The government troops pressed him. With his remaining twenty thousand men he marched out the west gate and formed a battle line with his back to the city, stretching seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang fled to Jiezhou, where government troops cornered him. He marched twenty thousand survivors out the west gate and formed a battle line seven li long, his back to the walls.

sentences.zh: 王令李世勣、程咬金、秦叔寶為北軍，翟長愻、秦武通為南軍。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered Li Shiji, Cheng Yaojin, and Qin Shubao to command the northern army; Zhai Changsun and Qin Wutong the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince deployed Li Shiji, Cheng Yaojin, and Qin Shubao on the north; Zhai Changsun and Qin Wutong on the south.

sentences.zh: 既戰，小卻，王以精騎突擊破之，金剛將輕騎去，賊將尉遲敬德、尋相、張萬歲降，收其精兵，遂復介州。

translations.literal: After the fighting began, they gave slight ground. The Prince then led elite cavalry in a sudden charge and broke them. Jingang fled with light cavalry. The rebel generals Yuchi Jingde, Xun Xiang, and Zhang Wansui surrendered. Their elite troops were taken into service, and Jiezhou was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: After a feigned retreat, the Prince drove his elite cavalry through their lines and broke them. Song Jingang fled with a light detachment. Yuchi Jingde, Xun Xiang, and Zhang Wansui surrendered; their best troops were absorbed, and Jiezhou was retaken.

sentences.zh: 武周引騎五百，棄并州，北走突厥。

translations.literal: Wuzhou led five hundred cavalry, abandoned Bingzhou, and fled north to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou abandoned Bingzhou with five hundred horsemen and fled north to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 金剛收散卒，將還拒，眾不為用，亦以百騎奔突厥。

translations.literal: Jingang gathered scattered soldiers, intending to return and resist, but the troops would not obey him, and he too fled to the Turks with a hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang rallied the scattered troops and meant to turn back and fight, but the men would not follow him, so he fled north to the Turks with a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 并州平，河東地盡復。

translations.literal: Bingzhou was pacified, and all the territory of Hedong was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou was secured, and every district of Hedong was restored to Tang control.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金剛背突厥，欲還上谷，為其追騎斬之。

translations.literal: Before long, Jingang turned against the Turks and wished to return to Shanggu; he was beheaded by their pursuing cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Song Jingang broke with the Turks and tried to return to Shanggu, but Turk pursuit riders caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 武周亦謀歸馬邑，計露，突厥殺之。

translations.literal: Wuzhou also plotted to return to Mayi; when the plan was exposed, the Turks killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou likewise plotted to return to Mayi, but when the scheme came to light the Turks put him to death.

sentences.zh: 起兵六年而滅。

translations.literal: Six years after raising troops, he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Six years after he first took up arms, his cause was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 先是，懷戎浮屠高曇晟因縣令具供，與其徒襲殺令，偽號大乘皇帝，以尼靜宣為耶輸皇后，建元法輪，遣使約開道為兄弟，封齊王，開道引眾從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Huairou monk Gao Tansheng, taking advantage of the magistrate's prepared provisions, together with his followers attacked and killed the magistrate, falsely styled himself Emperor of the Great Vehicle, made the nun Jingxuan his Empress Yesu, adopted the era name Falun, sent envoys to covenant with Kaidao as brothers, enfeoffed him as King of Qi, and Kaidao led his followers to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Huairou monk Gao Tansheng had used a feast the magistrate had prepared as his cover to strike with his disciples and kill the official. He proclaimed himself Emperor of the Great Vehicle, made the nun Jingxuan his Empress Yesu, and adopted the era name Falun. He sent envoys to treat Gao Kaidao as a sworn brother, enfeoffed him as King of Qi, and Kaidao brought his followers over to him.

sentences.zh: 居三月，殺曇晟，並其眾，復稱燕王，建元，署置百官。

translations.literal: After three months, he killed Tansheng, absorbed his followers, again styled himself King of Yan, established an era name, and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Three months later Kaidao killed Tansheng, took over his men, declared himself King of Yan again, set an era name, and installed a full court.

sentences.zh: 竇建德圍羅藝於幽州，藝請救，開道以騎二千赴之，建德解去，乃因藝使請降，詔以為蔚州總管、上柱國、北平郡王，賜姓李。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande besieged Luo Yi at Youzhou. Yi requested aid, and Kaidao went with two thousand cavalry to relieve him. Jiande lifted the siege and withdrew. Kaidao then sent envoys through Yi to request surrender. An edict appointed him Commander-in-chief of Wei Prefecture, Grand Pillar of State, and Prince of Beiping Commandery, and bestowed the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande besieged Luo Yi at Youzhou, Yi called for help and Kaidao rode to his relief with two thousand cavalry. Jiande broke off the siege and withdrew. Kaidao then used Yi's envoy to offer surrender. The court appointed him Commander-in-chief of Wei Prefecture, Grand Pillar of State, and Prince of Beiping Commandery, and granted him the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 開道以輕騎五百抵幽州，欲圖藝。

translations.literal: Kaidao reached Youzhou with five hundred light cavalry, intending to plot against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao arrived at Youzhou with five hundred light cavalry, planning to move against Yi.

sentences.zh: 自從數騎入都督府，且觀藝，藝與張飲盡歡，知不可圖，遂去。

translations.literal: He himself rode in with several attendants to the governorship to observe Yi. Yi spread a feast and drank with him to their heart's content. Realizing he could not be plotted against, Kaidao left.
translations.idiomatic: He rode into the governorship with only a few followers to take Yi’s measure. Yi entertained him generously and they drank together in full good humor. Seeing that Yi could not be trapped, Kaidao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，幽州饑，開道許輸以粟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Youzhou suffered famine; Kaidao promised to deliver grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Youzhou was stricken by famine, and Kaidao promised to send grain.

sentences.zh: 藝遣老弱湊食，皆厚遇之。

translations.literal: Yi sent the aged and weak to gather provisions, and all were treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent the old and weak to collect the grain, and Kaidao treated them all with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 藝悅，不為虞，更發兵三千、車數百、馬驢千往請粟，開道悉留不遣，遂北連突厥，告絕於藝，復稱燕，與劉黑闥聯兵入寇。

translations.literal: Yi was pleased and lowered his guard. He sent out three thousand more troops, several hundred carts, and a thousand horses and donkeys to request grain. Kaidao detained them all and would not send them back. He then allied with the Turks to the north, broke with Yi, again styled himself Yan, and joined forces with Liu Heita to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased by this, Yi dropped his guard and sent three thousand more troops, several hundred carts, and a thousand horses and donkeys to fetch grain. Kaidao kept them all and refused to release them. He then allied with the Turks in the north, broke with Yi, declared himself King of Yan again, and joined Liu Heita in raiding Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 開道攻易州不克，遣將謝棱詭降於藝，請兵應接。

translations.literal: Kaidao attacked Yizhou but could not take it. He sent his general Xie Ling to feign surrender to Yi and request troops for coordination.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidao failed to capture Yizhou and sent his general Xie Ling to pretend to surrender to Yi and ask for troops to coordinate with him.

sentences.zh: 藝眾至，棱縱擊破之，因導突厥俱南，恒、定、幽、易等騷然罹患。

translations.literal: When Yi's forces arrived, Ling launched a surprise attack and routed them, then guided the Turks south together. Heng, Ding, You, Yi, and other regions were thrown into uproar and afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi's men arrived, Xie Ling struck without warning and routed them, then led the Turks south together. Heng, Ding, You, Yi, and the surrounding districts were thrown into chaos and misery.

sentences.zh: 頡利以開道善攻具，與俱攻馬邑，拔之。

translations.literal: Illig, because Kaidao was skilled with siege equipment, joined him in attacking Mayi and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Illig Khan valued Kaidao's skill with siege engines and joined him in attacking Mayi, which they captured.

sentences.zh: 時群盜相繼平，開道欲降，自疑反覆得罪，猶恃突厥自安。

translations.literal: At this time the bandit leaders were pacified one after another. Kaidao wished to surrender but feared punishment for his repeated reversals; he still relied on the Turks for security.
translations.idiomatic: By then the other rebel chiefs had been subdued one after another. Kaidao wanted to surrender but feared punishment for his repeated betrayals, and still counted on the Turks to keep him safe.

sentences.zh: 然將士多山東人，思歸，眾益厭亂。

translations.literal: Yet his officers and soldiers were mostly from Shandong, yearning to return home; the troops grew ever more weary of the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his officers and men, however, were Shandong natives who longed to go home, and the army grew increasingly sick of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 初，開道募壯士數百為養子，衛閤下，及劉黑闥將張君立亡歸，開道命與愛將張金樹分督之。

translations.literal: Initially, Kaidao had recruited several hundred stalwart men as adopted sons to guard his headquarters. When Liu Heita's general Zhang Junli fled back to him, Kaidao ordered him and his trusted general Zhang Jinshu to jointly oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: At first Kaidao had recruited several hundred strong men as adopted sons to guard his headquarters. When Liu Heita's general Zhang Junli deserted back to him, Kaidao put him and his favorite commander Zhang Jinshu in joint charge of them.

sentences.zh: 金樹潛令左右數人偽與諸養子戲，至夕，入閤，絕其弓弦，又取刀槊聚床下。

translations.literal: Jinshu secretly had several of his attendants pretend to play with the adopted sons. At evening they entered the headquarters, cut their bowstrings, and gathered swords and spears beneath the beds.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu secretly ordered several of his attendants to pretend to play with the adopted sons. At dusk they entered the headquarters, cut the bowstrings, and piled swords and spears under the beds.

sentences.zh: 既暝，金樹以其徒噪攻之，數人者抱刀槊出閤。

translations.literal: Once night fell, Jinshu led his followers in a clamorous attack. The several men grabbed swords and spears and rushed out of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When night had fallen, Jinshu led his men in a noisy assault, and the few accomplices inside seized the swords and spears and burst out of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 諸義子將搏戰，亡弓槊。

translations.literal: The adopted sons were about to fight but found their bows and spears gone.
translations.idiomatic: The adopted sons tried to fight back, but their bows and spears were gone.

sentences.zh: 君立舉火外城應之，帳下大擾，養子窮，爭歸金樹。

translations.literal: Junli raised signal fires outside the city wall in response. There was great turmoil in the encampment; the adopted sons, at their wits' end, all turned to Jinshu.
translations.idiomatic: Junli lit signal fires outside the city to answer him, and the camp erupted in chaos. Cornered, the adopted sons one after another went over to Jinshu.

sentences.zh: 開道顧不免，擐甲挺刃據堂坐，與妻妾奏妓飲酒，金樹畏不敢前。

translations.literal: Seeing there was no escape, Kaidao donned armor, grasped his blade, and seated himself in the hall, having his wives and concubines perform music while he drank wine. Jinshu feared him and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no way out, Kaidao put on armor, drew his blade, and sat in the hall while his wives and concubines played music and he drank wine. Jinshu was afraid of him and did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 天且明，開道先縊其妻妾及諸子而後自殺。

translations.literal: As dawn approached, Kaidao first hanged his wives, concubines, and sons, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn neared, Kaidao hanged his wives, concubines, and sons first, then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 金樹羅兵取養子，皆斬之，亦殺君立而歸。

translations.literal: Jinshu gathered troops, rounded up the adopted sons, and beheaded them all. He also killed Junli and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshu mustered his troops, rounded up the adopted sons, and executed them all. He killed Junli as well and then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 開道起兵凡八年滅。

translations.literal: Kaidao's revolt lasted eight years in all before he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he raised troops to his fall, Kaidao's rebellion lasted eight years.

sentences.zh: 以其地為媯州，詔以金樹為北燕州都督。

translations.literal: His territory was made into Guizhou. An edict appointed Jinshu as Governor of Northern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His territory was reorganized as Guizhou, and an edict made Jinshu Governor of Northern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉黑闥，貝州漳南人。

translations.literal: Liu Heita was a native of Zhangnan in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heita was from Zhangnan in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒，喜蒱博，不治產，亡賴，父兄患苦之。

translations.literal: He was fond of drink, enjoyed gambling, did not manage property, and was a wastrel; his father and elder brothers were troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and gambling, never kept a trade, and was a good-for-nothing; his father and elder brothers were tormented by him.

sentences.zh: 與竇建德少相友，建德每資其費，黑闥所得輒盡，建德亦弗之計。

translations.literal: He had been friends with Dou Jiande since youth. Jiande regularly supplied him with funds; Heita always spent everything he received, yet Jiande never held it against him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Dou Jiande had been friends since they were young. Jiande kept giving him money, and Heita always spent every coin at once, yet Jiande never minded.

sentences.zh: 隋末，亡命從郝孝德為盜，後事李密為裨將。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui, he fled and joined Hao Xiaode as a bandit, later serving Li Mi as a subordinate general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he took to the roads, joined Hao Xiaode as a bandit, and later served Li Mi as a subordinate general.

sentences.zh: 密敗，王世充虜之，以其武健，補馬軍總管，鎮新鄉。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Wang Shichong captured him. Because of his martial prowess, he was appointed Commander of the Cavalry Army and stationed at Xinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi fell, Wang Shichong captured him. Impressed by his fighting skill, Shichong made him Commander of the Cavalry Army and posted him at Xinxiang.

sentences.zh: 時李世勣陷於竇建德，建德使攻新鄉，虜黑闥獻之，建德用為將，封漢東郡公。
