translations.literal: At that time Li Shiji had fallen into Dou Jiande's hands. Jiande sent forces to attack Xinxiang, captured Heita, and presented him as a prize. Jiande employed him as a general and enfeoffed him as Duke of Handong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Shiji was held by Dou Jiande, who sent troops against Xinxiang, captured Heita, and brought him in as a prize. Jiande put him in command and enfeoffed him as Duke of Handong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 黑闥與諸盜遊，素強武，多狙詐。

translations.literal: Heita consorted with various bandits, was innately fierce in battle, and full of stealth and trickery.
translations.idiomatic: Heita moved among the bandit chiefs, was naturally fierce in battle, and excelled at ambush and deceit.

sentences.zh: 建德有所經略，常委以斥候，陰入敵中覘虛實，每乘隙奮奇兵，出不意，多所摧克，軍中號為神勇。

translations.literal: Whenever Jiande undertook a campaign, he regularly entrusted Heita with reconnaissance. He would secretly enter enemy territory to observe conditions. Whenever he found an opening he would strike with exceptional troops, appearing where least expected, and won many crushing victories. The army called him divinely brave.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Jiande launched a campaign he usually put Heita in charge of scouting. Heita would slip into enemy lines to probe their strength, then at the first opening strike with a daring detachment from an unexpected direction and win crushing victories. The army called him divinely brave.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，建德敗，還匿漳南，杜門不出。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Jiande was defeated. Heita returned and hid in Zhangnan, shutting his door and not going out.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude, after Jiande's defeat, Heita went into hiding at Zhangnan and never left his house.

sentences.zh: 會高祖召建德故將範願、董康買、曹湛、高雅賢，將用之。

translations.literal: Just then the High Emperor summoned Ji's former generals Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, and Gao Yaxian, intending to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the High Emperor summoned Jiande's former generals Fan Yuan, Dong Kangmai, Cao Zhan, and Gao Yaxian, intending to put them in office.

sentences.zh: 願等疑畏，謀曰：「王世充舉洛陽降，驍將楊公卿、單雄信之徒皆夷滅。

translations.literal: Fan and the others were suspicious and afraid. They plotted, saying: "When Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang with his entire force, fierce generals like Yang Gongqing and Shan Xiongxin were all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and the others were suspicious and afraid. They plotted together, saying, "When Wang Shichong surrendered Luoyang with his whole army, fierce commanders such as Yang Gongqing and Shan Xiongxin were all wiped out.

sentences.zh: 今召吾等，若西入關，必無全。

translations.literal: Now that we have been summoned, if we go west into the Pass lands, we will certainly not survive intact.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have been summoned, if we go west into the Pass we will surely not come out alive.

sentences.zh: 且夏王於唐固有德，往禽淮安王、同安公主，皆厚遣還之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Xia owed Tang grace in the past—when he captured Prince Huai'an and Princess Tong'an, he sent them back with generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Prince of Xia had shown Tang kindness before: when he captured Prince Huai'an and Princess Tong'an, he treated them well and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 今唐得夏王，即加害。

translations.literal: Now Tang has the Prince of Xia and immediately harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Tang has the Prince of Xia in hand, they have already done him harm.

sentences.zh: 我不以余生為王得仇，無以見天下義士。」

translations.literal: If we do not spend our remaining lives avenging the Prince, we cannot face the righteous men under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not spend what life we have left avenging our prince, we will have no face to show the world's men of honor.

sentences.zh: 於是謀反。

translations.literal: Thus they plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: With that they resolved on rebellion.

sentences.zh: 卜所主，劉氏吉，共往見故將劉雅，告之，雅不從，眾怒，殺雅去。

translations.literal: They divined whom to follow; the Liu clan was auspicious. They all went together to see the former general Liu Ya and told him. Ya refused. The crowd was enraged, killed Ya, and left.
translations.idiomatic: They cast lots on whom to follow, and the Liu clan came up auspicious. They all went to the former general Liu Ya and told him their plan, but Ya refused. Enraged, the group killed him and departed.

sentences.zh: 範願曰：「漢東公黑闥果敢多奇略，寬仁容眾，恩結士卒。

translations.literal: Fan Yuan said: "The Duke of Handong, Heita, is resolute and bold, full of extraordinary stratagems, magnanimous in accepting men, and wins the loyalty of his troops through kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuan said, "The Duke of Handong, Heita, is resolute and bold, full of daring stratagems, generous to all who join him, and beloved by his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 吾嘗聞劉氏當王，今欲收夏王亡眾，集大事，非其人莫可。」

translations.literal: I have heard that the Liu clan is destined to rule. Now, wishing to gather the scattered followers of the Prince of Xia for a great undertaking, no one but him will do.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Liu clan is fated to rule. If we mean to rally the Prince of Xia's scattered followers for a great cause, no one else will serve.

sentences.zh: 乃之漳南，謁黑闥以告。

translations.literal: They then went to Zhangnan, visited Heita, and told him.
translations.idiomatic: So they went to Zhangnan, sought out Heita, and told him the plan.

sentences.zh: 黑闥喜，椎牛饗士，得兵百余人。

translations.literal: Heita was pleased. He slaughtered an ox to feast his men and gathered more than a hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Heita was delighted. He slaughtered an ox to feast his men and mustered more than a hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 襲漳南縣破之。

translations.literal: They raided Zhangnan County and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Zhangnan County and overran it.

sentences.zh: 貝州刺史戴元祥、魏州刺史權威合勢討擊，元祥等皆敗死，收其器械，有眾千人。

translations.literal: Beizhou Prefect Dai Yuanxiang and Weizhou Prefect Quan Wei combined forces to attack them. Yuanxiang and the others were all defeated and killed. Heita seized their weapons and had a force of a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Beizhou Prefect Dai Yuanxiang and Weizhou Prefect Quan Wei joined forces against him, but Yuanxiang and his colleagues were defeated and killed. Heita took their arms and raised his force to a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 建德故時左右稍歸之，兵浸盛。

translations.literal: Ji's former retainers gradually returned to him, and his army steadily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's old followers gradually rejoined him, and his army steadily swelled.

sentences.zh: 乃設壇漳南，祭建德，告以舉兵意。

translations.literal: He then set up an altar at Zhangnan, sacrificed to Jiande, and announced his intention to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised an altar at Zhangnan, offered sacrifice to Jiande, and declared his intent to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 自稱大將軍。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed himself Grand General.

sentences.zh: 陷歷亭，殺守將王行敏。

translations.literal: He seized Liting and killed the defending general Wang Xingmin.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Liting and killed the defending general Wang Xingmin.

sentences.zh: 饒陽賊崔元遜攻陷深州，殺刺史裴晞應之。

translations.literal: The Raoyang bandit Cui Yuansun attacked and seized Shenzhou, killed Prefect Pei Xi, and joined him.
translations.idiomatic: The Raoyang rebel Cui Yuansun stormed Shenzhou, killed Prefect Pei Xi, and rallied to Heita.

sentences.zh: 兗州賊徐圓朗亦相連和。

translations.literal: The Yanzhou bandit Xu Yuanlang also allied with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanzhou rebel Xu Yuanlang joined forces with him as well.

sentences.zh: 遂取瀛州，攻定州，殘之。

translations.literal: He then took Yingzhou, attacked Dingzhou, and ravaged it.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Yingzhou, attacked Dingzhou, and laid it waste.

sentences.zh: 乃移檄趙、魏，建德將吏往往殺令、尉附賊。

translations.literal: He then issued proclamations across Zhao and Wei. Ji's officers and officials often killed the magistrates and assistants and joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He issued proclamations across Zhao and Wei, and Jiande's former officers and officials often killed local magistrates and assistants and went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 北連高開道，勢雄張。

translations.literal: He allied with Gao Kaidao to the north, and his power swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He linked up with Gao Kaidao in the north, and his power expanded dramatically.

sentences.zh: 進至宗城，眾數萬。

translations.literal: He advanced to Zongcheng with a force numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward to Zongcheng at the head of a force numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 黎州總管李世勣戰敗，走洺州，黑闥追之，步卒五千皆覆，世勣挺身免。

translations.literal: Lizhou Commander-in-chief Li Shiji was defeated, fled to Mingzhou, and Heita pursued him. Five thousand foot soldiers were all wiped out; Shiji himself escaped by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhou Commander-in-chief Li Shiji was defeated and fled to Mingzhou. Heita pursued him, wiped out five thousand foot soldiers, and Shiji himself barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 乃以王琮為中書令，劉斌為中書侍郎，遣使北結突厥頡利，頡利遣俟斤宋邪那率騎從之，軍大振，不半年，盡有建德故地。

translations.literal: He then appointed Wang Cong as Director of the Secretariat, Liu Bin as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and sent envoys north to ally with the Turk Illig. Illig sent the yabgu Song Xiena leading cavalry to join him. The army was greatly invigorated. In less than half a year he held all of Jiande's former territory.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wang Cong Director of the Secretariat and Liu Bin Vice Director, then sent envoys north to treat with the Turk khan Illig. Illig sent the yabgu Song Xiena at the head of cavalry to join him. His army surged in strength, and in less than half a year he held all of Jiande's old territory.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔秦王及齊王元吉討之。

translations.literal: The High Emperor ordered the Prince of Qin and the Prince of Qi, Yuanji, to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor ordered the Prince of Qin and Prince of Qi Yuanji to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 五年，黑闥陷相州，號漢東王，建元天造，以範願為左僕射，董康買兵部尚書，高雅賢為左領軍，王小胡為右領軍，召建德僚屬，悉復用之，都洺州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Heita seized Xiangzhou, styled himself King of Handong, adopted the era name Tianzao, appointed Fan Yuan as Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai as Minister of War, Gao Yaxian as Left Army Director, Wang Xiaohu as Right Army Director, summoned Ji's staff, restored them all to office, and made his capital at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Heita took Xiangzhou, declared himself King of Handong, and adopted the era name Tianzao. He made Fan Yuan Left Vice Director, Dong Kangmai Minister of War, Gao Yaxian Left Army Director, and Wang Xiaohu Right Army Director, recalled Jiande's former staff and put them all back in office, and established his capital at Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦王率兵次汲，數困賊，進下相州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin led troops to camp at Ji, repeatedly harassed the rebels, and advanced to descend upon Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin led his army to Ji, repeatedly harried the rebels, and pressed down on Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 棣州人復殺刺史叛歸黑闥。

translations.literal: The people of Dizhou again killed their prefect and rebelled to return to Heita.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Dizhou again killed their prefect and went over to Heita.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦王破之於列人，取洺水，使總管羅士信守之。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Prince defeated them at Lieren, took Ming River, and had Commander Luo Shixin hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Prince defeated them at Lieren, seized Ming River, and left Commander Luo Shixin to hold it.

sentences.zh: 黑闥攻陷洺水，士信死。

translations.literal: Heita attacked and seized Ming River; Shixin died.
translations.idiomatic: Heita stormed Ming River and killed Shixin.

sentences.zh: 王阻水為連營，分奇兵絕其饋路。

translations.literal: The Prince blocked the river with linked encampments and sent detached forces to cut off their supply lines.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince blocked the river with a chain of camps and sent flanking troops to sever the rebel supply lines.

sentences.zh: 黑闥數挑戰，堅壁不為動。

translations.literal: Heita repeatedly challenged battle, but the Prince held his walls and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Heita repeatedly offered battle, but the Prince kept his walls and would not be drawn out.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊糧盡，王度必決戰，豫壅洺水上流，敕吏曰：「須賊度，亟決之。」

translations.literal: In the third month, the rebels' grain was exhausted. The Prince reckoned they would surely fight a decisive battle. He beforehand dammed the upper reaches of the Ming River and instructed officials: "When the rebels cross, break the dam at once.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels' grain ran out. The Prince judged that they would have to fight a decisive battle, so he dammed the upper Ming River in advance and told his officials, "When the rebels cross, break the dam at once.

sentences.zh: 黑闥果率騎二萬絕水陣，與王師大戰，眾潰，水暴至，賊眾不得還，斬首萬余級，溺死數千，黑闥與範願等以殘騎奔突厥。

translations.literal: Heita indeed led twenty thousand cavalry to cross the water and form battle lines. He fought a great battle with the Prince's army. The rebels were routed. The water surged forth suddenly; the rebel host could not return. More than ten thousand heads were taken, several thousand drowned. Heita with Fan Yuan and others fled to the Turks with the surviving cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Heita duly led twenty thousand cavalry across the river into battle against the Prince's army. His force collapsed as the water burst through; the rebels could not get back across. More than ten thousand heads were taken and several thousand drowned. Heita fled to the Turks with Fan Yuan and the other survivors.

sentences.zh: 山東平，秦王還。

translations.literal: Shandong was pacified; the Prince of Qin returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong was pacified, and the Prince of Qin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 黑闥藉突厥兵復入寇，攻定州。

translations.literal: Heita, relying on Turk troops, raided again and attacked Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heita borrowed Turk troops and raided again, attacking Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊將曹湛、董康買先逃鮮虞，聚兵應之。

translations.literal: Former generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai had earlier fled to Xianyu and gathered troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: His old generals Cao Zhan and Dong Kangmai had already fled to Xianyu and were gathering troops to answer his call.

sentences.zh: 帝以淮陽王道玄為河北總管，與原國公史萬寶討賊，戰下博，敗績，道玄死於陣，萬寶輕騎逸，繇是河北復叛歸賊。

translations.literal: The Emperor appointed Prince Huaiyang Daoxuan as Commander-in-chief of Hebei, and together with Duke of Yanguo Shi Wanbao attacked the rebels. They fought at Xiabo and were defeated. Daoxuan died in battle; Wanbao escaped on light cavalry. Thereupon Hebei again rebelled and returned to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor put Prince Huaiyang Daoxuan in command of Hebei and sent him with Duke of Yanguo Shi Wanbao against the rebels. They fought at Xiabo and were routed; Daoxuan died on the field and Wanbao escaped on a fast horse. Hebei then rebelled again and went back to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 黑闥仍都洺州。

translations.literal: Heita again made his capital at Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Heita again made Mingzhou his capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，略瀛州，殺刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he raided Yingzhou and killed the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he raided Yingzhou and killed the prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔齊王元吉擊之，不進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Qi Yuanji to attack him, but he did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Prince of Qi Yuanji to attack him, but Yuanji would not move.

sentences.zh: 又詔皇太子督兵並力，頻戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the Crown Prince to supervise the troops and combine forces; they won repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict put the Crown Prince in overall command and combined the armies; they won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 十二月，皇太子、齊王悉兵戰館陶，黑闥大敗，引軍走，躡北至毛州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi deployed all their troops and fought at Guantao. Heita was badly defeated, withdrew his army, and fled. They pursued north to Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi brought their full strength to battle at Guantao. Heita was routed and fled; the Tang forces pursued him north as far as Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 黑闥整眾，背永濟渠陣，縱騎搏之，賊赴水死者數千，黑闥遁去。

translations.literal: Heita re-formed his forces, formed battle lines with the Yongji Canal at their backs, and sent cavalry to charge. Several thousand rebels drowned in the water. Heita slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Heita rallied his men and drew up with the Yongji Canal at their backs, then sent cavalry to strike. Several thousand rebels drowned trying to escape, and Heita slipped away.

sentences.zh: 騎將劉弘基追蹙，賊不得休。

translations.literal: Cavalry commander Liu Hongji pressed the pursuit closely; the rebels could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Liu Hongji pressed the pursuit so hard the rebels could not catch their breath.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，馳至饒陽，騎能屬者才百余，困且餒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, he galloped to Raoyang. Only a little over a hundred horsemen could keep up. They were exhausted and hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he raced to Raoyang with barely a hundred horsemen still able to follow, exhausted and starving.

sentences.zh: 黑闥所署總管崔元遜迎拜，延之入。

translations.literal: Cui Yuansun, whom Heita had appointed commander, came out to receive him with obeisance and invited him in.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuansun, the commander Heita had appointed, came out to greet him with obeisance and invited him into the city.

sentences.zh: 黑闥不許，元遜固請，且泣，乃進城下。

translations.literal: Heita would not agree. Yuansun pressed his invitation and wept; only then did Heita approach below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Heita refused, but Yuansun pleaded again and wept until Heita finally came up beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 元遜饋之，方飯，車騎諸葛德威勒兵前，黑闥罵曰：「狗輩負我！」

translations.literal: Yuansun offered him food. While he was just eating, Cavalry General Zhuge Dewei led troops forward. Heita cursed: "You dogs have betrayed me!
translations.idiomatic: Yuansun brought him food. While he was still eating, Cavalry General Zhuge Dewei advanced at the head of his troops. Heita cursed, "You dogs have betrayed me!

sentences.zh: 遂執詣皇太子所斬之。

translations.literal: They seized him and brought him to the Crown Prince's headquarters, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him, brought him before the Crown Prince, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 德威舉郡降，山東遂定。

translations.literal: Dewei submitted the entire commandery. Shandong was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei surrendered the whole commandery, and Shandong was finally settled.

sentences.zh: 余黨及突厥兵間道亡，定州總管雙士洛邀戰，破平之。

translations.literal: The remaining followers and Turk troops fled by hidden routes. Dingzhou Commander-in-chief Shuang Shiluo intercepted and fought them, defeating and pacifying them.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels and Turk soldiers fled by back roads, but Dingzhou Commander-in-chief Shuang Shiluo intercepted them, defeated them, and restored order.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王建天策府，其弧矢制倍於常。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Prince of Qin established the Heavenly Stratagem Office, his bow and arrows were made twice the normal size.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin first established the Heavenly Stratagem Office, his bow and arrows were made twice the usual size.

sentences.zh: 逐黑闥也，為突厥所窘，自以大箭射卻之。

translations.literal: When pursuing Heita, he was hard pressed by the Turks and personally used his great arrow to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: While pursuing Heita he was cornered by Turks and personally drove them back with one of his great arrows.

sentences.zh: 突厥得箭，傳觀，以為神。

translations.literal: The Turks obtained the arrow and passed it around for all to see, regarding it as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks recovered the arrow and passed it from hand to hand, marveling at it as something supernatural.

sentences.zh: 後余大弓一、長矢五，藏之武庫，世寶之，每郊丘重禮，必陳於儀物之首，以識武功雲。

translations.literal: Later one great bow and five long arrows remained. They were stored in the armory and treasured through the generations. Whenever the grand rites at the suburban altars were performed, they were invariably displayed at the head of the ceremonial objects, as a mark of martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: One great bow and five long arrows remained afterward. They were kept in the armory and treasured for generations; at every grand suburban rite they were placed at the head of the ceremonial regalia as a token of martial glory.

sentences.zh: 徐圓朗者，兗州人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuanlang was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang was a man of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末為盜，據本郡，以兵徇瑯邪以西，北至東平，盡有之，勝兵二萬，附李密。

translations.literal: At the end of the Sui he became a bandit, held his home commandery, marched his troops west as far as Langya, and north to Dongping, holding all of it. His battle-ready troops numbered twenty thousand. He attached himself to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he turned bandit, seized his home commandery, and marched west as far as Langya and north to Dongping until he held the whole region with twenty thousand fighting men, then attached himself to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密敗，歸竇建德。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he submitted to Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi fell, he went over to Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 山東平，授兗州總管、魯郡公。

translations.literal: When Shandong was pacified, he was appointed Commander-in-chief of Yanzhou and Duke of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Shandong was pacified he was made Commander-in-chief of Yanzhou and Duke of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣葛國公盛彥師安輯河南，抵任城，會黑闥兵起，圓朗執彥師應之，自號魯王，黑闥以為大行臺元帥。

translations.literal: The High Emperor sent Duke of Ge Sheng Yanshi to pacify Henan. When he reached Rencheng, Liu Heita's rebellion broke out. Yuanlang seized Yanshi and joined him, styled himself King of Lu, and Heita made him Marshal of the Grand Expeditionary Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor sent Duke of Ge Sheng Yanshi to pacify Henan. When he reached Rencheng, Liu Heita's rebellion broke out. Yuanlang seized Yanshi and joined him, declared himself King of Lu, and Heita made him marshal of the Grand Expeditionary Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 兗、鄆、陳、杞、伊、洛、曹、戴等州豪桀皆殺吏應賊，秦王已破黑闥，遣兵屯濟陰經略之。

translations.literal: Magnates of Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, Dai, and other prefectures all killed officials to join the rebels; the Prince of Qin had already broken Heita and sent troops to garrison Jiyin and pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Local strongmen across Yan, Yun, Chen, Qi, Yi, Luo, Cao, Dai, and neighboring prefectures killed their officials and rallied to the rebels. The Prince of Qin had already defeated Heita and sent troops to hold Jiyin and bring the region under control.

sentences.zh: 圓朗懼。

translations.literal: Yuanlang grew afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang was alarmed.

sentences.zh: 河間人劉復禮說圓朗曰：「彭城有劉世徹，才略不常，有異相，士大夫許其必王。

translations.literal: Liu Fuli of Hejian urged Yuanlang, saying, "At Pengcheng there is Liu Shiche—his talent and stratagems are extraordinary, his physiognomy unusual, and the gentry say he is destined to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fuli of Hejian advised Yuanlang, "At Pengcheng there is a man named Liu Shiche—brilliant and unpredictable, with the look of a born ruler. The educated class already say he is destined for the throne.

sentences.zh: 將軍欲自用，恐敗，不如迎世徹立之，功無不濟。」

translations.literal: If you, General, wish to act on your own, I fear you will fail—better to welcome Shiche and set him up as ruler; your enterprise cannot then fail."
translations.idiomatic: If you try to hold power yourself, General, you will probably lose. Welcome Shiche and make him your sovereign instead, and you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 圓朗謂然，乃迎之。

translations.literal: Yuanlang thought this right and went to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang agreed and went to receive him.

sentences.zh: 盛彥師以世徹若聯叛，禍且不解，即謬說曰：「聞公迎劉世徹，信乎？

translations.literal: Sheng Yanshi, seeing that if Shiche were joined in rebellion disaster would be hard to undo, at once spread a false report, saying, "I hear you are welcoming Liu Shiche—is it true?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yanshi feared that if Shiche were brought in, the rebellion would become unstoppable. He spread a rumor at once: "I hear you are welcoming Liu Shiche—is that true?

sentences.zh: 公亡無日矣！

translations.literal: Your days are numbered!
translations.idiomatic: Your end is near!

sentences.zh: 獨不見翟讓用李密哉？」

translations.literal: Have you alone not seen how Zhai Rang employed Li Mi?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you forgotten what happened when Zhai Rang brought in Li Mi?"

sentences.zh: 圓朗信之。

translations.literal: Yuanlang believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlang believed him.

sentences.zh: 世徹至，奪其兵，以為司馬，遣徇地，所至皆下，忌而殺之。

translations.literal: When Shiche arrived, Yuanlang seized his troops, made him Marshal, and sent him to reduce territory—wherever he went all submitted—but out of jealousy killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiche arrived, Yuanlang stripped him of his troops, made him marshal, and sent him to conquer the countryside. Every place he reached submitted, but Yuanlang grew jealous and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 會淮安王神通、李世勣合兵攻圓朗，圓朗數敗，總管任環遂圍兗州，降者爭逾城。

translations.literal: When Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and Li Shiji combined forces to attack Yuanlang, Yuanlang was repeatedly defeated; Area Commander Ren Huan then besieged Yanzhou, and those who surrendered scrambled over the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'an Li Shentong and Li Shiji joined forces against Yuanlang. He lost battle after battle. Area Commander Ren Huan besieged Yanzhou, and defectors scrambled over the walls to surrender.

sentences.zh: 圓朗窮，棄城，與下數騎夜亡，為野人所殺。

translations.literal: Yuanlang, driven to extremity, abandoned the city and fled by night with a few horsemen; country folk killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Yuanlang abandoned the city and fled by night with only a handful of horsemen. Country people caught and killed him.
